tasks.title: Ack-based coalescing and dispatch on the user-input queue
tasks.change: A move or wheel leaves at once if none is in flight; later ones coalesce into one slot (latest move, summed wheel per phase) sent on the ack; keys and clicks pass at once; host dispatches via cmux_shim_post_user_input_task, wheel via send_wheel with phase and momentum, and acks at dispatch. Hand-off from p04-input-065: the host posts every input task through 065's InputTasks (ChromiumHost/src/host_user_input.h, `input_tasks` in browser_host_main.mm): HostInput's Post is `[&input_tasks](std::function<void()> task) { input_tasks.Post(std::move(task)); }`, and PostInputTask with its per-post PostToMain fallback goes. The queue is chosen once at start: the fork's user-input queue, else CefPostTask(TID_UI); the main run loop until CefInitialize returned (input_tasks.Start()). A refused task (Chromium's UI thread shut down) is dropped: its batch keeps the BatchGate shut until HostInput::Stop. Test: chromium_host_input_ring_test TestHostInputThroughInputTasks.

tasks.title: Report visible host windows; install the blocked-widget handler
tasks.change: At startup, before any page is detached, call cmux_set_blocked_widget_handler (176, API 31); each report becomes BLOCKED_WIDGET {browser id, kind, Views class, rect, visible, owner}. The cmux UIs that own a kind (062 permission prompts, 063 JS dialogs, 228 choosers, find) take their requests through their own shim events before Chromium makes a widget, and the fork cannot hand a made widget to a cmux UI, so a reported widget is a request its owner missed: the host dismisses it with cmux_blocked_widget_close (Chrome's Escape) and logs it, except a permission prompt, whose Escape PermissionRequestManager records as a dismissal toward the origin's embargo (PermissionDecisionAutoBlocker): it is held unanswered (logged held) until Chromium ends it. Backstop for what the fork cannot block (window-modal sheets, AppKit panels): before the main run loop waits, in every mode, order out any host window ordered in with alpha > 0 and report UNEXPECTED_WINDOW {class, title hash}. The bench counts BLOCKED_WIDGET by class and owner, UNEXPECTED_WINDOW, and the host pid's on-screen windows with alpha > 0 (CGWindowList) per native-ui row.

Spec applies all 3 reviews (each claim checked with git grep at 772cdfc45ac).

p11-codebase.program: p11-codebase: Chrome-style component codebase (F13). CmuxNextApp (143,911 lines) becomes a composition root of <= 10k lines in Composition/Hosts/Launch/Menus, with scopes AppFeatures/MachineFeatures/WindowFeatures/WorkspaceFeatures/TabFeatures and one sanctioned ProcessRoot. Feature code sees WorkbenchInterface protocols, never the hub concretes. 0 stateful singletons by type, 0 app broadcast names, 0 broadcast observers outside CmuxNextEnvironment, 0 hard/soft/upward edges, 0 mixed targets. A mirror-tree DEPS checkdeps built on check-package-dependency-lists.py refuses regressions before push. Leaf-edit incremental build < 30 s, measured from hour 0. Machine queues are generated from an SCC-condensed app graph. Each move is a seam commit plus a pure move commit, landed through a fleet merge train; Package.swift is touched only by the scaffold and an hourly manifest agent. Owner-gated hot files (Phase W) run last.

plan.capacity_math:
Tasks: about 2,150 cards after the ranges are expanded, about 1,950 after dedupe. About 70% touch Swift (1,350), about 20% Rust (400) and about 10% scripts or docs.

Swift compile cost on an aws-m4pro host with a warm cache: a touched-target package build takes 4-6 min. The CmuxNextApp target alone is 143,911 of the 636,401 Swift lines and dominates any edit that reaches it. An --app build takes 10-12 min (perf-lead: 725 s for a cold build with setup; seed cold Swift 275 s). Budget 6 min per compile job and 2 concurrent jobs per 14-core host (memory-bound), which gives about 15 jobs per host-hour after contention.

Swift demand: each card needs about 4 compiles (implementer 2, fixer 1.5, train share 0.5), so 1,350 x 4 = 5,400 compiles over the H8-H52 window, an average of 123/h with peaks near 250/h. That is about 17 hosts at peak. Filtered swift test runs add about 1.5 per card, roughly 2,000 runs of 8 min each: about 4 more hosts. The merge train needs 3 dedicated hosts (build, test, bisect). The hourly Release compile-check needs 1. Total build pool: about 25 Macs at peak. The Linux Swift tier (p15) moves maybe 15-20% of package type-checks to the VM after H24; that is upside, not something to plan on.

Rust: 400 cards x 4 builds. cargo check takes 6-20 s, workspace clippy 3-5 min, nextest 10-15 min. The 360-core VM runs about 24 isolated target dirs of 15 cores each, with a shared sccache. That is about 140 clippy or test runs per hour against a demand of about 40/h, so it has room. Reserve 120 cores for fuzz, sanitizers and mutants from H40. About 15% of Rust work is macOS-only (kqueue, mach sampler, holder), which adds about 1 Mac.

GUI and perf benches need a console session and a 120 Hz virtual display. Demand:
- perf-lab T0 on alternate 10-min batches, about 20 min of shards each: 2 hosts full time.
- T1 every 3 h: 1 host.
- Pinpoint bisect and verification: 2 hosts.
- Test-phase done checks: 15 programs x about 15 sessions x 20 min = about 75 host-hours inside 12 h: 6-7 hosts.
- A/A and reference: 1 host.
That is 10 GUI hosts (minimum 8); today there is 1. Tart macOS 14/15 VMs need 2 more Apple-silicon hosts in the test phase. CEF fork trains need 2 dedicated large-memory Macs for a 4-6 h Chromium mac build per train.

Total: about 25 build + 10 GUI + 2 Tart + 2 fork = about 39 Macs. Owned today: aws-m4pro-1..9 (9), the M6 minis cmux15-24 without cmux20 (9), and a few named hosts (cmux8s, cmux10s, cmux20-bench, cmux-austin-mini-0), about 22 in all. Plan: turn the 9 M6 minis into auto-login GUI bench hosts and use aws-m4pro plus rented hosts for builds. That leaves about 17 Macs to rent for 72 h (EC2 Mac hosts have a 24 h minimum allocation). Without them, the plan shrinks to about 150 agents and the test phase loses about 8 h.

Agent count follows compile supply, not tokens: about 350 concurrent agents at peak need about 17 hosts for compiles alone, because each agent compiles about once per 10-15 min of writing.

needs_owner: Money for build and bench capacity. Reply `rent 17 EC2 Mac hosts for 72 h (about $2,500; plan runs at about 350 agents)` or `rent 8 EC2 Mac hosts (about $1,200; writing peak queues, test phase loses about 8 h)` or `rent none (plan shrinks to about 150 agents and many done checks stay unmeasured)`.

Use of the 9 owned M6 minis (cmux15-24 without cmux20). Reply `convert all 9 to auto-login GUI bench hosts with a 120 Hz virtual display for the 72 h (they stop taking build jobs)` or `convert only 4 (perf lab T0 and T1 run; test-phase done checks run 2-3x slower)`.

Window pictures saved to disk at quit, so the next launch shows a picture first (p08-057..063; terminal and page text then sits on disk, with incognito and password fields filled). Reply `on by default with the privacy fills and a setting to turn it off` or `off by default; launch shows the material background until live content draws`.

Energy Saver default (p14-022; Chrome's model: caps page frame rate at 30, makes motion loops static, stretches background polls, shows a sidebar indicator; your typing is never throttled). Reply `auto when on battery at or below 20% (Chrome's default)` or `off unless you turn it on in Settings`.

Memory Saver default (p07-065; discards hidden browser tabs, cmux pages, chats and terminal GPU frames after Chrome's timeouts, and shows a picture until a discarded item reloads). Also restores the 15-min idle unmount of parked workspaces (takes back 6f04ec90105). Reply `balanced mode on by default, the 15-min parked timeout back (Chrome's default)` or `off by default; only memory pressure discards`.

Remote kill switch (p12-093/094): the app fetches a signed flags.json next to the release notes, which can turn a cmux feature off on installed apps without an update. Reply `allow remote turn-off for Nightly and Release` or `Nightly only` or `no remote control; features change only with an update`.

Aggregate performance data upload (p09-134, p12-152): latency, hang, launch and idle histograms with no URLs, keys or paths, plus Nightly field trials (2-arm A/B of a feature). Reply `Release opt-in prompt plus Nightly field trials` or `Nightly only, no Release prompt, no field trials`.
top_risks: Build capacity is the true ceiling. A CmuxNext touched-target compile takes 4-6 min and an app build 10-12 min. At about 350 agents the Swift compile demand peaks near 250 jobs/h, about 17 hosts for compiles alone (about 25 Macs with tests and the merge train). Without rented hosts, the queues grow and the 72 h plan slips. Mitigation: compile only touched targets, a batched merge train, a warm cache per host, the Linux Swift tier after H24, and capping agents to compile supply.

Only 1 GUI host with a desktop session today. Nearly every done check (key->frame, motion drops, idle wakeups, launch, the Chromium host rows) needs a console session and a 120 Hz display. If 8-10 GUI hosts are not ready by H8, there are no baselines and the test phase cannot prove any target.

The CEF fork train is on the critical path. One Chromium Mac build takes 4-6 h, plus signing and publishing. The p01 host-mode parity rows (IME bounds, select, autofill, drag, choosers), p03 visibility and fence, p13 page groups and renderer-less spare, and the p14 saver all wait on train 1 (cut H26, pin H36). A broken train leaves host mode default-off and several idle and memory targets unmet. Mitigation: CEFForkFeatures gates with the old path kept, a fixes-only train 2.

Duplicate designs and hot files. HangWatch exists 4 times, Rust QoS 6 times, the launch fence 3 times, plus the coalescer, input tap, discard planner, wire generator, crash keys, loop visibility and the Track B vs host-mode conflict. If the H0 dedupe in ownership_conflicts is not enforced, agents build parallel primitives and the merge train spends its time on conflicts. Mitigation: H0 DAG publish, lease registry, hot-file splits, queues regenerated after every merge.

Mass mechanical sweeps change runtime behavior in ways a diff-only reviewer cannot see: moving work off main changes ordering, panic denies change error paths, unowned to weak changes lifetimes. Examples are the p06 FG300-346 sweeps, p02 raw-blocking, p10 unchecked/panic/SAFETY, p14 timers and p11 seams. Mitigation: the daemon oracle by H12 and the app oracle by H20 before the sweeps peak, a base..head diff on every train batch, a regression test red at base for each behavior fix, and trap-mode sweeps in the test phase.

p11 moves about 130k lines out of CmuxNextApp, the same files that p01, p03, p04, p06, p07, p08, p13 and p15 edit. Even with follow-renames, Phase W (Windows, Focus, Drag, Pages, NewTab) can freeze half the fleet or regress the input path (CMO, hot code crossing modules). The App <= 10k target is likely to end at the H48 checkpoint (<= 60k); that is the accepted floor.

Out-of-process Chromium and the VT worker processes are risk:high: signing and identity, TCC attribution, IME/AX/native UI parity across about 25 native UI kinds, crash-restore, minidumps, sandbox. 72 h is short for 100% native-ui on macOS 14/15/26/27. Expect host mode to stay default-off in Release and Nightly at H72 unless every row passes; the risk:high receipts need independent review on the exact head.

Some targets cannot be proven in 72 h of wall time. The p10 field metrics need 3 days of nightly-next, readiness-soak needs 24 h, long-day-soak needs 8 h, and the Release field data has to come from people. These are cut to 6 h soaks and stated as cut. Some numeric targets (launch warm <= 150 ms, STRESS key->frame p99 <= 16.7 ms, app+daemon idle <= 1/s with Chromium tabs) may end as measured gaps rather than passes. The report must give the real numbers, not claims.

Infra single points of failure built in the first 8 h: merge train, lease registry, manifest agent, perf lab labd, oracle runnerd. Each has one owner. If any breaks during the H12-H40 peak, landing stops for everyone. Mitigation: a fallback of direct pushes in small, serial, lease-checked batches, and a standby owner for each.

drift on feat-cmux-next and the agent rules. Other agents keep landing on feat-cmux-next, and the 2-hourly merges collide with Phase W and the manifest agent. With hundreds of agents, the CLAUDE.md rules (no local compiles on the person's Mac, never --no-verify, no new CI gates or steps, never quit the running cmux) will be broken somewhere unless the agent brief and the PATH guards enforce them.

On memory.limit warning or critical and 30 s after a STRESS teardown, call malloc_zone_pressure_relief (macOS) or malloc_trim (Linux), or mi_collect if the A/B picks mimalloc. memory-report.py --pid <daemon> adds a fragmentation row (vmmap --summary: allocated vs resident in the malloc zones).
missing_tasks.acceptance: The allocator choice is one cfg in main.rs, with the A/B numbers in the commit. The relief call runs on a utility thread from cmux-threads, never on a request or echo thread (the reviewer checks the spawn). A test covers the relief trigger.
missing_tasks.test_phase: memory-soak 2 h STRESS: after teardown, daemon RSS is within 10 % of its pre-STRESS value; fragmentation (resident minus allocated) <= 15 %; the daemon slope stays <= 5 MB/h.

missing_tasks.title: Staged Nightly rollout with automatic halt on crash or hang rate (Omaha staged rollout)
missing_tasks.change: AppcastSelector reads an optional rollout percentage per item and a stable per-install bucket (a random value stored once, never sent anywhere). rollout-halt.py (an operator tool, not CI) reads stability-health.py for the newest Nightly. When crash-free sessions are < 99.5 % or there are > 2 own hang events >= 2 s per 100 session-hours, it publishes a flags.json halt that pins the previous item. Nothing today stops a bad Nightly once it is published, so with hundreds of agents landing, the 'fix forward' rule needs a brake. risk:high (updater).
missing_tasks.acceptance: A unit test of the selector at 0/10/50/100 % with fixed buckets. Halt pins the previous item. A missing or invalid rollout field means 100 % (the old behavior). The bucket value is in no network request (the reviewer greps the request builders). The diff adds no workflow file.
missing_tasks.test_phase: Updater suite on the fleet; a dry run of rollout-halt.py against the last 3 nightly-next releases prints the decision it would have made.

missing_tasks.title: Page-load parity story: FCP/LCP/CLS/INP in cmux Chromium tabs vs Google Chrome at the same revision (PageLoadMetrics)
missing_tasks.change: A lab story that replays the p12 WPR corpus (30 sites: news, docs, apps, video) in a cmux Chromium tab (in-process and host mode) and in Google Chrome Stable at the closest revision. It reads the PerformanceObserver largest-contentful-paint, paint, layout-shift and event entries through CDP. This catches what cmux adds per load (the pump, layer hosting, document scripts, built-in ad blocker, page bridge), which no current target measures. p12's Speedometer row covers JS only.
missing_tasks.acceptance: The story writes result-v1 rows named page_load.<metric>.<engine-mode>, with 0 network misses from the WPR replay required for a valid row. The URL list is a checked-in JSON file. The reviewer checks that the Chrome arm runs with a fresh profile and the same flags.
missing_tasks.test_phase: T2 run on 2 GUI hosts: LCP p50 cmux <= Chrome + 5 %, FCP p50 <= Chrome + 5 %, CLS equal, for both cmux modes; host mode no worse than in-process.
depends_on: p12 Web Page Replay for Chromium tabs

missing_tasks.title: Omnibar speculative preconnect and prerender (Chrome's AutocompleteActionPredictor), to beat Chrome on typed navigations
files: Manaflow CEF fork include/cef_cmux.h + libcef/browser/cmux_preconnect.cc (fork train 1 entry)
missing_tasks.change: Fork export cmux_cef_preconnect(url, count) (content PreconnectManager) and cmux_cef_prerender(url) (speculation rules prerender into the active profile). The omnibar calls preconnect when the top suggestion's confidence is >= 0.5 and prerender at >= 0.8 (Chrome's action predictor thresholds), at most 1 prerender. It cancels on Esc, on hidden or on Energy Saver. Gate in CEFForkFeatures.
missing_tasks.acceptance: Thresholds and caps are named constants with unit tests. No speculation in incognito or while saver is on. Old pins keep the old path (the CEFForkFeatures check is visible in the diff).
missing_tasks.test_phase: crit-006 story with omnibar-typed navigations to 10 corpus URLs at 100 ms RTT: navigation-to-FCP p50 at least 30 % lower than without speculation and <= Chrome's; omnibar key->frame p99 stays <= 16.7 ms.

missing_tasks.title: Chromium host wire: fuzz targets on both sides and the bad_message rule
missing_tasks.change: p01 builds a generated control channel and an input ring between cmux and the Chromium Host, and p05 and p10 fuzz every other wire, but nothing fuzzes this one. Add a libFuzzer target over the host-side decoder (generated from gen-chromium-host-wire.py, so all N ops and M event kinds are reachable), a Swift CmuxFuzzSupport suite over the app-side decoder, and the rule from Chrome's bad_message: an invalid frame from the host ends the host (supervisor restart, counted), never cmux.
missing_tasks.acceptance: The fuzzers take their dictionary from chromium-host-ops.json. The app decoder has no force-unwrap, trap or index on wire lengths without a check (the reviewer checks the decoder diff). A test sends 5 malformed frame kinds and sees one host-kill per frame and the app alive.
missing_tasks.test_phase: Each fuzz target runs >= 1 h with -fork from a stored corpus: 0 crashes, OOMs or timeouts; chromium-host-bench --kill-host shows a bad-message restart in the crash page path.

missing_tasks.title: Shared Swift compilation cache across fleet hosts (Chrome RBE/Siso analog) and sccache for Rust on Macs
missing_tasks.change: Build capacity is the plan's top risk (about 39 Macs, 22 owned). Turn on Swift 6.2 compile caching (-cache-compile-job with a CAS) for touched-target fleet builds, with a CAS directory shared per host and a remote cache service on the 360-core VM. Add sccache with a shared bucket for cargo on the Macs. Measure the hit rate and wall time before compile capacity decides the agent count.
missing_tasks.acceptance: The script and host config only. No change to Package.swift build settings for Release. Off with one env var. The receipt format records cache_hits, cache_misses and wall_s per job.
missing_tasks.test_phase: The same SHA built on 2 aws-m4pro hosts one after the other: second-host touched-target wall time -50 % and hit rate >= 80 %; a 1-line leaf edit rebuild is no slower than without the cache; Release compile-check output is identical (dSYM UUIDs aside).

missing_tasks.title: Rust leaf-edit build target and a crate-split queue for cmux-tui-core (378k lines in one crate)
missing_tasks.change: The target 'incremental build after a leaf edit < 30 s' has a Swift done check (p11) but only 'dated numbers' for Rust. cmux-tui-core is 377,973 lines in one crate, so any edit recompiles all of it. Add a <30 s pass/fail to bench-edit-loop-rust.py (probes: a core leaf module, server/, mux/, cmux-holder, cmux-tui cli). rust-crate-split-queue.py reads the core module graph (use/mod edges), condenses SCCs and prints the extraction order, one task per crate (<= 400 moved lines of glue per task, pure moves separate). This replaces the single p11 'Resume the cmux-tui-core crate split' card.
missing_tasks.acceptance: The queue generator is deterministic (same output twice). Every emitted line names a module set and its target crate. The bench prints p50 and max per probe and exits non-zero above 30 s only with --check.
missing_tasks.test_phase: bench-edit-loop-rust.py --check on the VM and an aws-m4pro host: body-only edit in a core leaf module p50 < 30 s after the extractions (base number recorded at hour 0).
missing_tasks.machine_queue: rust-crate-split-queue.py output: one task per extracted crate

missing_tasks.title: lifecycle-sweep.py: the tool p02 RUN-1/RUN-12 and p10 need
missing_tasks.change: The repo has no lifecycle-sweep tool (git ls-files: none), but p02 RUN-1 and RUN-12 and the p02 test-phase task require one with traps. Build it with steps: launch cold (daemon stopped + purge) and warm, quit, sleep and wake (pmset schedule wake on an exclusive host, or the injected-clock path), display add and remove (scripts/ci/frame-pacing/vdisplay.m), appearance toggle, daemon kill -9 and reconnect, Chromium renderer and GPU crash, and the update-install dry run. Each step records traps from debug.blocking and hangs from debug.hangs, and the run exits non-zero on any trap.
missing_tasks.acceptance: Each step is a function with its own pass rule. --steps selects a subset. The report is result-v1. No step touches /Applications/cmux.app or com.cmuxterm.app (the reviewer checks the bundle-id guard).
missing_tasks.test_phase: Fleet Debug run with CMUX_BLOCKING_TRAP=1 exits 0 on the head; on the base it reports the traps it finds (red-before evidence).

missing_tasks.title: Native-UI fixture corpus and drivers for chromium-host-bench --native-ui, part 1: forms and pickers
missing_tasks.change: chromium-host-bench.py takes only --modes, --count and --stress today. The p01 done row --native-ui (about 25 kinds) has no fixtures and no drivers. Part 1 covers select, datalist, date/time, color, autofill, password and the file picker, served by the p15 hermetic fixture server. Each driver opens the control by a real click, picks a value through the cmux-drawn UI (AX press), and reads the result back from the page through CDP.
missing_tasks.acceptance: One fixture and one assertion per kind. The driver checks that the host is never frontmost and that no host window is visible (CGWindowList alpha > 0). Each row reports pass, fail or not-supported, never skipped silently.
missing_tasks.test_phase: Host mode and in-process mode on macOS 26/27: 100 % pass of the part-1 rows in both modes.
depends_on: p15 Hermetic local web fixture server

missing_tasks.title: Native-UI drivers part 2: permissions, devices and media (virtual devices through CDP)
missing_tasks.change: Drive the permission prompts, WebAuthn (CDP WebAuthn.addVirtualAuthenticator), device choosers (CDP DeviceAccess and BluetoothEmulation), screen share and camera (--use-fake-device-for-media-stream in the bench config only), external protocol and Web Share. Without virtual devices these rows cannot run on a fleet Mac.
missing_tasks.acceptance: The fake-device switches go only into the bench CEF switch file and never into a shipping CEFSwitches extension (the reviewer checks). One assertion per kind.
missing_tasks.test_phase: 100 % of the part-2 rows in host mode on macOS 26/27.

missing_tasks.title: Native-UI drivers part 3 and the IME driver: windows, fullscreen, print, DevTools, PiP, locks, Kotoeri, dead keys, emoji
missing_tasks.change: Part 3 covers JS dialogs, HTTP auth, cert error, beforeunload, print, extension popup, DevTools docked and undocked, window.open, PiP, fullscreen, pointer lock, keyboard lock and swipe. The IME driver selects the input source with TISSelectInputSource (Kotoeri Romaji, ABC Extended for dead keys), types through CGEvent and opens the emoji picker with orderFrontCharacterPalette plus an AX press. Dictation cannot be automated in a VM, so that row is driven through a test-only insertText injection and is labeled 'injected'.
missing_tasks.acceptance: Every p01 --ime and --native-ui row maps to exactly one driver function (the reviewer checks the mapping table in the file header). The dictation row is labeled injected, not real.
missing_tasks.test_phase: --ime on Tart 14/15 and fleet 26/27: Kotoeri, dead key and emoji 100 %; firstRect < 0.1 ms; ime_sync_requests == 0.

missing_tasks.title: Release-build blocking census (the target is 'in Release'; the detector is compiled out of Release)
missing_tasks.change: p02 RUN-11 removes the detector from Release, and the DYLD-inserted probe needs an entitlement Release does not have. Today no tool measures blocking calls in the shipped configuration. Record Release with xctrace (System Call Trace plus Thread State Trace on the main thread) during the every-action sweep light and STRESS. Classify off-CPU main intervals >= 1 ms by their first cmux frame, using the existing report's symbolication and owner lookup.
missing_tasks.acceptance: The script needs no change to the Release build. The report reuses blocking-probe-report.py grouping (one code path for both inputs). Its output has a release_main_blocking_sites count.
missing_tasks.test_phase: Fleet Release, light and STRESS: release_main_blocking_sites == 0 outside the named CefInitialize entry (pre-F2); the number goes into perf-lead.md section 5.
depends_on: p02 TEST PHASE: blocking probe app and daemon

missing_tasks.title: TUI and web frontend latency and idle (daemon-side frontends have no target)
missing_tasks.change: cmux-tui ships a Rust TUI frontend and a web frontend, and no program measures their key->echo, render cost or idle wakeups. Add a PTY-driven bench that writes a key to the TUI and timestamps the byte that redraws the cell (Linux VM and macOS), and a Chromium-driven bench for the web frontend (key event -> rAF after the DOM change). Both also report idle wakeups over 60 s.
missing_tasks.acceptance: Both benches write result-v1. Neither changes frontend code. The TUI bench runs headless on the VM.
missing_tasks.test_phase: TUI key->echo p99 <= 16.7 ms with 10 printing panes; idle 0 wakeups/s from the TUI process; web frontend key->rAF p99 <= 16.7 ms.

missing_tasks.title: Terminal throughput and CPU per GB: beat standalone Ghostty and Terminal.app
missing_tasks.change: Measure cat of a 1 GB mixed file, `yes`, and a vtebench-like corpus (dense SGR, unicode, scroll regions). Report wall time and CPU-seconds per GB summed over app + daemon + holder + VT workers, and key->frame in a sibling pane during the flood, against Ghostty.app and Terminal.app on the same host. The holder, VT pool, D3 rings and app-draws-screens change this path completely, and no target guards its cost.
missing_tasks.acceptance: The bench sums per-process CPU with proc_pid_rusage, and reports each reference app and its version. The report is result-v1.
missing_tasks.test_phase: Fleet: cmux CPU-s/GB <= 1.3 x standalone Ghostty and <= Terminal.app; sibling-pane key->frame p99 <= 16.7 ms during the flood; base vs head recorded.

missing_tasks.title: Disk-write budget while active (Chrome ImportantFileWriter coalescing; macOS EXC_RESOURCE disk-writes limit)
missing_tasks.change: p14 D15 checks 0 bytes only at idle. Nothing bounds writes during a STRESS storm, for example journal fsyncs per op (210 fsync/sync_all sites in 113 Rust files), session saves or caches. Measure ri_diskio_byteswritten and the fsync count per process kind over a 60-min STRESS plus CLI storm, and project to 24 h against the macOS disk-writes resource limit.
missing_tasks.acceptance: The report has bytes_per_hour, fsyncs_per_op and bytes_per_keystroke per process kind; read-only bench.
missing_tasks.test_phase: app + daemon <= 100 MB/h in STRESS storm; 0 fsyncs per keystroke; a 24 h projection under 1/4 of the EXC_RESOURCE limit.

missing_tasks.title: Rust perf-hot markers and benches (daemon parity with the Swift perf-hot rule)
missing_tasks.change: Rust has 2 perf-hot markers (cmux-kitty-media) and perf-hot-benches.json lists no Rust bench. Mark the daemon hot paths (PTY read, holder ring write, VT parse per chunk, output frame encode, request dispatch, journal append, mux fan-out) with `// perf-hot: <budget> <path-id>`, add criterion benches with a lang field in the JSON, and let the pre-push hook name them the same way as Swift.
missing_tasks.acceptance: Every new marker has a JSON row and a bench function of the same id (the reviewer checks the 1:1 mapping). The benches print numbers and have no time asserts.
missing_tasks.test_phase: cargo bench on the VM records each path's p50/p99 at base and head; no hot-path regression > 5 %.
missing_tasks.machine_queue: rg -n 'perf-hot:' cmux-tui --type rust (2 today) vs the list of hot paths in threading-model.md

missing_tasks.title: Heavy-session launch target (Chrome measures session restore with many tabs)
missing_tasks.change: p08 measures --profile realistic only. Add --profile heavy (150 workspaces, 172 terminals, 20 Chromium tabs, 5 windows) built through perf-stress-session.py, with the same milestones and order checks.
missing_tasks.acceptance: Profile definition in one place, reused by process-model-census --session heavy (the reviewer checks there is no second fixture).
missing_tasks.test_phase: Warm heavy: first_window_frame_committed p50 <= 200 ms; first_live_content_frame p50 <= 400 ms; main turn p99 <= 4 ms in the 2 s after first frame; cold numbers recorded.

missing_tasks.title: Merge-train admission precheck and speculative parallel batches (Chrome CQ / Zuul)
missing_tasks.change: At about 45 card merges an hour plus fixer commits, a 15-min batch of 11-15 commits with even a 5 % individual red rate is red about 45 % of the time, so the train bisects most of the time. A branch enters the train only with a fleet receipt for its own SHA: a touched-target compile, its tests and the daemon oracle when Rust changed. Batches run speculatively: batch N+1 builds on top of N while N is being checked, and a red batch is bisected by parallel halving on the 3 train hosts.
missing_tasks.acceptance: Admission refuses a branch whose receipt SHA is not its head. The speculation and bisect logic has unit tests with fake build results: a red in the middle of a batch of 12 is found in <= 4 rounds.
missing_tasks.test_phase: A dry run of the last 24 h of feat-cmux-next pushes through the train: the computed batch-red rate and the queue latency go into the plan.

missing_tasks.title: Land into feat-cmux-next in per-program waves from H24, not one H70 merge
missing_tasks.change: The tool cuts the trunk into PRs every 8 h, one per program, split by risk tier. It writes each PR's risk label, its 'Takes back #N' lines (for example p07's 6f04ec90105), its Observed / Not run section from the receipts, and its regression-test red and green commands. It uses merge commits, not squash, so the red-before-fix commits stay. A single 2,000-commit PR at H70 cannot carry an exact-head SHIP receipt that means anything, and its risk:high items would hold everything else.
missing_tasks.acceptance: Each generated PR is under 400 changed files and contains one program and one risk tier. The tool refuses to emit a PR that mixes tiers or has no receipts.
missing_tasks.test_phase: A dry run on the trunk at H24 lists the PRs it would open; the reviewer subagent checks one low-tier and one normal-tier PR body.

missing_tasks.title: In-process CEF browser-process fatal: automatic relaunch with restore (Release while host mode stays off)
missing_tasks.change: The plan expects host mode to stay off in Release and Nightly at H72, so 'a Chromium crash never ends cmux' stays false there: a browser-process CHECK ends the app. Until F2 ships, catch the CEF FATAL path (the log handler plus a crash-key write), save the window and tab state through the existing quit-save path's async-signal-safe subset, and relaunch through a launchd-submitted one-shot. Terminals survive in the daemon and holder; tabs come back from PageState. Add a crash-matrix kind cef-browser-check-inproc.
missing_tasks.acceptance: The handler calls only async-signal-safe functions (the reviewer checks against a listed allowlist). The relaunch is skipped in crash-streak safe mode (p08). One relaunch per 5 min at most.
missing_tasks.test_phase: crash-matrix cef-browser-check-inproc: cmux is back with every terminal screen within 2 s and tabs with URL and scroll within 3 s; 4th crash in 5 min starts in safe mode.

missing_tasks.title: Program guardrail rules run only locally: CI's guardrails.py call skips the local tier
missing_tasks.change: .github/workflows/cmux-next-fast-gates.yml and cmux-next.yml run guardrails.py and prepush-gate.py. So every rule the programs add (p02 pool-blocking and task-priority, p03 sync-layout, p04 input-monitor, p06 rules, p11 checkdeps, p14 wakeup-ext, p15 switch warning) becomes a CI gate unless it is marked otherwise, against Lawrence 2026-10-23. Before any program rule lands, rules under guardrails/rules/<program>.py get tier=local by default. A CI run (detected from the env the workflows already set) loads only the existing tier. No workflow file changes.
missing_tasks.acceptance: `guardrails.py --list` shows a tier column. With CI=true set, `--list` shows no program rule. A unit test covers both. git diff of .github/workflows is empty.
missing_tasks.test_phase: The pre-push hook on a dev worktree reports a seeded violation of a local rule; the same command with CI=true does not.

problems.problem: About 38 of the measuring tools are missing at 772cdfc45ac (checked with git ls-files and git grep). problems.problem: No program covers: accessibility performance with an AT client attached (Chrome AXMode); GPU device loss for cmux's own Metal renderers (Chrome GPU restart, only Chromium's GPU is covered); allocator purge and fragmentation for the Rust daemon (PartitionAlloc purge; no shipped Rust binary sets an allocator); staged rollout with automatic halt (Omaha); page-load metrics vs Chrome (PageLoadMetrics; Speedometer covers JS only); omnibox speculation (AutocompleteActionPredictor); fuzzing of the new Chromium host wire (Mojo fuzzers plus bad_message); a shared compile cache (RBE/Siso), which the capacity math needs most.

The app has a perf-hot rule with benches (21 Swift markers); Rust has 2 and perf-hot-benches.json lists no Rust bench. The TUI and web frontends have no latency or idle target. No target covers terminal throughput or CPU per GB through the new holder, VT pool and ring path, or disk writes while active (210 fsync sites in 113 Rust files).
problems.fix: Add crit-016, crit-017, crit-018 and crit-019.

problems.problem: Cold and warm launch are measured only with --profile realistic. Session restore of a heavy session (150 workspaces, 20 tabs) is where Chrome's TabLoader work matters, and it has no target.

problems.where: Cards a diff-only reviewer cannot judge: p14 'Root cause of hidden main wakes (107/s)' and 'Q9 slot A/B/C: next IDLE-BUDGET-OVER owner'; p04 'Day-1 input hotspots on the base'; p05 'Q9 triage'; p06 'Spike (decision gate): priority-ordered main executor hook'; p03 spikes 013/014; p13 spikes 028/051/089/090; p01 'The app draws terminal screens (spike, then build)'; every 'TEST PHASE' card
problems.problem: These cards have no diff whose correctness a reviewer can check. Their output is a measurement or a decision.

The reviewer then checks the numbers against the stated rule. A spike has a deadline hour and a default branch that applies if it slips.
